report.summary: All three UI failures are the same Page.goto timeout on /books at the 5 s limit. The cause is an artificial random delay of 0–8 s in app/main.py list_books(), which runs on every /books render, so roughly 3 in 8 page loads exceed the timeout. Fix the app code first (remove or bound the sleep), and treat these tests as flaky until then.

causes.title: /books page render sleeps a random 0–8 s, exceeding the 5 s goto timeout
causes.explanation: list_books() calls time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) before querying the database. render_books() calls list_books() for every /books page render, so the HTML response is delayed by a random amount. The shared fixture sets the default timeout to 5000 ms (tests/ui/conftest.py:5-7), and BooksPage.open() calls page.goto('/books') with the default 'load' wait (tests/support/pages.py:33-35). When the random delay exceeds about 5 s, goto times out before the page loads. Outcomes depend on chance, so the same commit can pass on a rerun. The app is not wrong about the data; the delay is simply nondeterministic. The login UI tests did not fail because they navigate to /login, which does not call list_books. The assertions in the three failing tests were never reached.
evidence: app/main.py:256: "books": list_books(user["id"]),  (called from render_books on every /books render)
tests/ui/conftest.py:5-7: fail_fast sets page.set_default_timeout(5000) with the comment 'Nothing in this app should take longer than 5 s'
Failure text (all three tests): "Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: navigating to \"http://127.0.0.1:49185/books\", waiting until \"load\""
Only one time.sleep/random call exists in app/ or tests/ besides the 0.2 s poll in tests/conftest.py:41, so this is the sole delay source.
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the random sleep from app/main.py:150 (it appears to be a debugging or fault-injection leftover, and the app is meant to be fast per the conftest comment). If the slowness is intended as a test scenario, make it deterministic and test it explicitly, and do not let it leak into the default /books render. As a secondary hardening step, have BooksPage.open() wait for a stable element (e.g. the books list or current-user) rather than relying solely on the 'load' event and the 5 s default. Do not raise the timeout as the only fix, since the delay can still exceed any fixed limit.
